newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-INSIGHT - Aussie clears one hurdle, $0.7960 next.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-INSIGHT - Aussie clears one hurdle, $0.7960 next.

text.p: The Australian dollar's uptrend has strengthened significantly after U.S. and Swiss bank buying gave it a bullish offshore finish atop US$0.7940 resistance.

The break opened the way for a re-test of October's high around US$0.7980/85 on route to the crucial barrier of US$0.7990/00. Dealers said there were a clustre of offers in the way at US$0.7960 resistance, but momentum was in the currency's favour as were developments on the fundamental side.
Japanese demand for high yielders remained strong with no sign of rates there rising, the CRB index and copper had bounced and US$/yen seemed to have found a bottom at 111.00 yen.
By 8.15 am (2115 GMT) the dollar poised at US$0.7944/49, its highest local start since October 22, having made the important move to US$0.7940/45 Tuesday from US$0.7910/14 the day before.

Immediate support was lined up at US$0.7925 but some analysts saw a risk the currency had completed the first rise of a three wave sequence from the US$0.7815 low of November 8. If so, a pullback to 79 cents or even US$0.7865/70 was likely before the next leg of its uptrend.
The longer term outlook would become clearer on a test of the US$0.8000/8020 band, which marked peaks of several failed rallies since it made a five year top of US$0.8050 in May.
A break above this barrier would ignite a new multi-month uptrend with 84 cents as an achievable target, analysts said. Failure would imply a correction back to US$0.7815.

On the crosses the AUD was holding up at 88.64/74 having rallied almost a yen to 88.67/77 late Tuesday. It also recouped ground on the mark and Swiss franc thanks to an ongoing switch to higher yielding currencies like the AUD and sterling.

The risk of another easing in domestic rates had not faded completely but was distant enough -- few saw much chance of a move before March -- to keep the dollar attractive for now. Crucially, there was no feeling Japanese rates would rise soon.
That might change if the Bank of Japan's Tankan survey on November 27 proved a lot stronger than expected, although market rumour so far was tipping a weak outcome.
Domestic data were thin on the ground with the Westpac leading index for September the only figure of note today.

Elsewhere, commodity prices were mixed but with pockets of strength, notable copper which shot to five-month highs Tuesday. The Commodity Research Bureau futures index continued its recent bounce rising 1.04 points to 245.51, putting it comfortably above the November 5 trough of 235.99 but still far below the April peak of 263.79. -- Wayne Cole 61-2 9373 1800
